description: A graph whose facts (edges) carry validity time, used as agent memory so changes over time are explicit.
Two independent timelines per fact: valid time (when it was true) and transaction time (when the system believed it).
`validFrom`/`validTo`: the period in which a fact held in the world.
`recordedAt`/`expiredAt`: the period in which the memory believed a record. It makes past beliefs auditable.
Closing a contradicted fact (expiring it and recording its end) instead of deleting or overwriting it.
A relation a subject can have only one value for at a time, such as `works_at`. A new value contradicts the old one.
"What was true at T, as known at K?": filter by valid time and transaction time.
Zep's open-source temporal knowledge graph engine for agent memory: episodes, entities and facts with valid, invalid, created and expired timestamps.
Deciding that different mentions ("Ana", "Ana Souza", "she") refer to one node. Errors here corrupt a graph memory.
